This class is for the student and teacher to have a little chat and get to know one another, it is not a sample class and I will not be teaching a regular class during the trial, the trial class is meant to discuss goals, expectations, learning styles and interests so that I can design your learning plan.

Next, I discuss their personal interests and hobbies which help me put together a learning plan that will be interesting for the student. pro_course_detail.title: Conversational/Free Speak
pro_course_detail.description:
In this "Free Speak", relaxed style of class, we talk about various different topics ranging from current events to personal interests of the student. This speaking time is great for the teacher to listen to and identify pronunciation, grammar and vocabulary mistakes and allows a relaxed and laid back approach to corrections!
Note: Please make sure that you speak in more than one or two words, this class is meant for the student to talk and be heard.

pro_course_detail.title: Accent Reduction (North American Neutral Accent)
pro_course_detail.description:
As of 3/29/2024 I will only be offering 45 and 30 minute classes of this specific lesson. If you have already booked 1 hour lessons, we will continue to do those until the end of your package. 
In these lessons, I break down each of the sounds that ESL students struggle with the most. We use diagrams, mouth positioning exercises and listening exercises to really get into the physical reason behind why accents happen. I emphasize and practice intonation and cadence in class. I focus on helping the student perfect the pronunciation of some of the most difficult sounds in the English language such as "schwa", long & short vowel sounds, consonant endings and the dreaded "r" sound amongst others.

pro_course_detail.title: General/Writing English Lessons with Material Provided
pro_course_detail.description:
In these general English lessons I provide the materials for the student. We work on listening, speaking, vocabulary, reading, writing and grammar exercises. Each lesson is taught surrounding a particular topic and I aim to tailor the class topics according to the students' interests, for example, if a student likes Art, I try to provide Art related lessons.
We go over each exercise together where I explain, answer questions, correct pronunciation and have speaking moments with the student. Book a trial with me!

pro_course_detail.title: Business English/Career English/Professional English/Work Related English
pro_course_detail.description:
In these classes I provide the study material to the student and we work on business vocabulary, business idioms and business phrasal verbs. We discuss business situations, for example, leading a meeting or making an appointment. 
We also learn how to write business emails and do listening and speaking exercises. Last but not least, I teach students about business etiquette and business culture in the United States.

pro_course_detail.title: English for Lawyers and Law Students and Job Interview Preparation
pro_course_detail.description:
Learn legal English and prepare for a job interview at an American law firm!
I have extensive experience in the job interview process as I have interviewed and hired several different candidates in my past career in the Legal field. In these classes we use my experience to prepare the student for their upcoming interview. We learn how to write proper resumes and cover letters. 
We practice how to answer questions properly, proper etiquette and what to ask. I also do several mock interviews with the student where I provide feedback so the student can improve every weak point.

pro_course_detail.description:
We'll follow a proven curriculum that will help you advance your English and get you feeling confident as soon as possible! Ideally this syllabus includes 45 minute classes twice a week for ten weeks on your schedule.

These lessons will be tailored to your specific needs.

Curriculum:
Week 1: Pronunciation - common mistakes for your language, review of vowels and consonants 
Week 2: Grammar - differences between common verb tenses
Week 3: Vocabulary - false cognates in your language, expanding vocabulary
Week 4: Conversation - phrasal verbs 
Week 5: Listening - blending
Week 6: Pronunciation - word stress (compound words, schwa)
Week 7: Grammar - prepositions 
Week 8: Vocabulary - root words, switching registers 
Week 9: Conversation - idiomatic expressions 
Week 10: Listening - understanding native speakers

exp_info.description: Over the past 18 months, I have gained invaluable experience in teaching English as a Second Language online. I have taught over 600 lessons to students of all ages and abilities, including small children, students learning English for work, students learning English to live in America, and much more. I have developed a unique method for optimal learning, which includes a mixture of conversational and structured practice, with lessons designed specifically for each student.

As the owner of my own online store on Teachers Pay Teachers, I create, develop, and sell digital printable educational resources to teachers around the globe. One of my store's specializations is ESL/EFL resources and lesson plans.

Working as an Environmental Education Intern at Lums Pond State Park, I had the opportunity to educate people of all ages and backgrounds on the beautiful nature surrounding them. I helped run a large variety of educational programs, covering topics such as animal species found in the pond, tree identification, monarch butterfly habitat/migration/conservation, kayaking tours, and much more. I helped people find their passion for the natural world around them.

While pursuing my degree in Zoo Keeping Technology, I completed 700 hours of volunteering in the Education Department at Cheyenne Mountain Zoo. In my role as a Junior Zoo Keeper, I spent much of my time speaking and presenting to Zoo guests, educating them about our animals. I gave talks to groups of all sizes and ages about our animals' care, their anatomy, and our Zoo's role in conservation.

I spent three summers as a volunteer at my local library. I was a part of multiple library programs during my time there, including: Summer Reading Program, Reading Buddies (reading books with young children), and general library duties.

While attending Colorado Springs Early Colleges, I was chosen to be part of our school's National Honor Society. This prestigious group was in charge of carrying out service projects in our community, such as food drives for the homeless.

In my final year of middle school, I was chosen to be part of a program called WEB "Where Everybody Belongs". In this program, I helped 6th graders have a smooth transition into middle school. Our WEB group (all 8th graders) spent time with the kids during their first week of school and checked in on them throughout the year. We helped them do homework, talked to them about their transition, showed them around the campus, and led them in some fun games to help them get to know each other.
